A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ECHO research work, with readable main text and Appendices A–D. Pages 2–21 have identical extracted text and rendered images; first-page differences are confined to author attribution and the arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original ECHO experiments, including speedups and accepted-token counts in Table 1, throughput and ablations in Figure 5, and confidence-distribution analyses in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix D, including benchmark measurements, ablations, and confidence-distribution analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain identical sparse confidence gating, calibration, and elastic budget scheduling procedures. No method component or inference step changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HumanEval, GSM8K, CNN/DM, Alpaca, and MT-Bench with the same task coverage and low- and high-concurrency scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same model-specific comparator membership, including Lookahead, Sps, Medusa, Hydra, OPT-Tree, DDD, and EAGLE3. Figure 5 retains EAGLE3 and the same two ECHO variants.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the same model configurations, greedy decoding, 1024-token generation limit, batch sizes, evaluation metrics, and framework settings.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 retains the sparse-versus-dense gating and depth-aware-versus-fixed threshold ablations. Figure 4's utilization analysis and Appendix D's confidence-distribution analyses are also identical.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains the same per-request percentile reporting: 25th–75th percentile boxes and 5th–95th percentile whiskers. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-test information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results, and reported findings match. For example, Table 1 retains ECHO's 5.35x HumanEval speedup with LLaMA3.3-70B and 2.02x average speedup with Qwen3-235B, both at batch size 1.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Theorems 1–2, and Appendix A's Proposition 1, assumptions, and derivations are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about sparse gating, elastic scheduling, SGLang integration, and acceleration across model scales and concurrency regimes.

C2.justification: The interpretations involving verification bottlenecks, gating errors, and budget reallocation are unchanged. Appendix A's qualification that width expansion improves coverage without guaranteeing immediate depth progress and Appendix D's confidence-drift explanation are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical hardware, precision, model identifiers, CUDA-Graph settings, calibration thresholds, and tree configurations. Both versions state that source code will be made available later.

R1.justification: Section 6, Appendix B, and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning relative to speculative decoding methods and serving schedulers.

P1.justification: v2 adds an equal-contribution asterisk to Baolin Zhang in the author list and updates the first-page arXiv version/date stamp. The prose, terminology, and section and appendix structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9, Tables 1–2, Algorithm 1, captions, and their placement are unchanged. The first-page attribution and stamp edits preserve the existing page arrangement.

improvement.justification: v2 updates equal-contribution attribution and the arXiv stamp while preserving all scientific content, evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information, including the appendices. These administrative edits do not establish a meaningful change in overall paper quality.
